title: A weird race for second place

Survey arithmetic showing Robredo (24%) ahead of the combined challengers (16%)
Defense of contrast (Marcos vs Robredo) as voter-benefit, not disadvantage
FLP Scholarship 2021 bar results -- 22 scholars all passed (100% tradition upheld)
sub_topics: Lacson, Isko Moreno, Bert Gonzales joint press conference dispelling withdrawal rumors and asking Robredo to step aside
Pacquiao's absence from the presser despite 6% survey share

stances.claim: The Lacson-Moreno-Gonzales joint demand that Robredo withdraw is mathematically incoherent -- her 24% Pulse Asia share exceeds the trio's combined 10% (and 16% even with Pacquiao's 6%) -- so if anyone should withdraw, it should be them, not her.
stances.rhetorical_move: survey-arithmetic counter-argument (simple addition refutes the strategic premise)

stances.claim: The Marcos-Robredo contrast in programs and personalities is a bonus to voters, not a disadvantage -- giving them a real choice rather than a homogeneous field.
stances.rhetorical_move: reframing contrast as benefit (turns the trio's premise on its head)

stances.claim: CJ formally demotes Senator Lacson from 'top of his presidential choices' to 'bottom of his short list' because of this presser -- a rare on-the-record consequence in a retired jurist's seldom-partisan column.
stances.rhetorical_move: explicit-personal-consequence disclosure (rare in CJ's typically reticent partisan voice)

stances.claim: Marcos's deliberate absence has degenerated the TV/Comelec debates into 'pitiful debates for the second place' -- diminishing voter information.
stances.rhetorical_move: metaphorical-degradation diagnosis (institutionalized debates 'pitiful' without the frontrunner)

stances.claim: The 100% bar passing rate of 22 FLP scholars, with 14 rated 'Excellent' or 'Exemplary' under the SC's new top-tier classifications, validates the rigor of the FLP screening committees and boards of judges -- particularly the strong showing of outside-Metro-Manila law schools (UCor, USC, FSUU).
stances.rhetorical_move: tradition-of-excellence framing with regional-equity bonus (geographic diversity as institutional virtue)

notable_anecdotes: Three presidential aspirants (Lacson, Moreno, Gonzales) held a hyped press conference asking Robredo to withdraw -- CJ does the math out loud and shows their combined 10% is less than half her 24%.

Lacson had been at the top of CJ's presidential short list 'given his undisputed experience in the public service and his tenacious stand against corruption especially the pork barrel and its reinventions' -- the presser flipped him to the bottom, a rare on-the-record demotion from a retired jurist.

The SC changed its bar-results practice: no top-10 announcement, instead 'Excellent' (>90%) and 'Exemplary' (85-90%) tiers -- CJ uses this new vocabulary to celebrate FLP scholars under the new schema.

Three FLP 'Excellent' rated examinees all came from outside Metro Manila: Stephanie Mae Domingo (UCor-Baguio), Geremae Mata (USC-Cebu), Jani Omamalin (USC-Cebu) -- CJ highlights this as a regional-equity success.
Full named list of 22 scholars + 10 dissertation winners reproduced in the column -- operating as both tribute and historical record of FLP impact.

one_paragraph_summary: Two weeks before Election Day 2022, Panganiban -- opening with the disclaimer that as a retired jurist he 'seldom write[s] on highly partisan matters' -- critiques the joint press conference at which Senator Ping Lacson, Manila Mayor Isko Moreno, and former defense secretary Bert Gonzales asked Vice President Leni Robredo to withdraw and let voters consolidate behind one of them as the viable alternative to Bongbong Marcos. He does the survey arithmetic out loud: Lacson (2%) + Moreno (8%) + Gonzales (0%) + an absent Pacquiao (6%) = 16%, still well below Robredo's 24%, so 'logically then, if anyone should withdraw, it should be the four, not the VP'; the Marcos-Robredo contrast in programs and personalities is a 'bonus to voters,' not a disadvantage. He formally demotes Lacson from the top of his presidential short list to the bottom because of the presser, and laments that Marcos's debate-skipping has reduced the televised forums to 'pitiful debates for the second place.' The column pivots via star-bar transition to a 'more pleasant topic': all 22 FLP scholars (in partnership with Tan Yan Kee Foundation) passed the 2021 bar, with 3 rated 'Excellent' (>90%) and 11 rated 'Exemplary' (85-90%) under the Court's new tier classifications, while 10 FLP-Ayala Dissertation Writing Contest winners also rated 'Exemplary.' He highlights the strong showing of UCor (Baguio), USC (Cebu), and FSUU (Butuan) as regional-equity evidence and closes with the April 30 deadline for the next cohort at www.libpros.com.
